boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named University of Cincinnati spaces for studying, connecting, reflection, and student programming on Main Campus.

cards.title: Tangeman University Center
cards.subtitle: 2766 UC MainStreet
cards.notes: Use the powered seating on levels 3 and 4 between classes, or coordinate a group session in the food-court seating; request an open meeting room when needed.
cards.short_summary: A central MainStreet building with casual seating, food-court tables, and on-demand group rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: UC identifies TUC as a place to eat, shop, study, and meet; it says powered furniture is available on levels 3 and 4 and groups gather in the food court to study.
cards.access_notes: UC states that everyone is welcome in TUC; meeting-room availability and on-demand requests vary.

cards.title: Bearcat Plaza
cards.subtitle: Outside Tangeman University Center on MainStreet
cards.notes: Bring a classmate and use the outdoor steps during suitable weather for a quick review session or a pause before heading back inside TUC.
cards.short_summary: The outdoor steps by MainStreet offer an informal extension of TUC study space.
cards.evidence_claim: TUC’s study-spaces page specifically points students to the steps outside on MainStreet and Bearcat Plaza during nice weather.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor use is weather-dependent; consult campus conditions before planning to stay.

cards.title: Walter C. Langsam Library
cards.subtitle: Central library, Main Campus
cards.notes: Choose a setting to match the task: use the living room for flexible seating, reserve a group room with UC credentials, or look for a table on an upper floor.
cards.short_summary: UC’s central library combines individual study, small-group work, technology, and library help.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Libraries says Langsam offers spaces for learning, studying, creating, small-group work, and breaks between classes, including reservable study rooms and common areas.
cards.access_notes: Study-room booking requires UC credentials; UC notes that entry after the desk closes requires UC affiliation and Bearcat Card/photo ID.

cards.title: Langsam Living Room
cards.subtitle: Fourth floor, Walter C. Langsam Library
cards.notes: Settle into the fourth-floor seating when you want a flexible study base near the library’s services, then move to a reservable room if your group needs one.
cards.short_summary: A fourth-floor seating and study area within Langsam Library.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Libraries describes the Langsam Living Room on the fourth floor as providing a variety of seating and study spaces.
cards.access_notes: Located inside Langsam Library; library building access policies apply.

cards.title: Prayer and Meditation Room
cards.subtitle: Langsam Room 451, Walter C. Langsam Library
cards.notes: Use this quiet room for prayer or reflection, and keep the visit focused on its stated purpose rather than treating it as a general meeting space.
cards.short_summary: A quiet fourth-floor room for prayer and reflection, created with Student Government.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Libraries identifies Langsam Room 451 as a Prayer and Meditation Room for prayer and reflection, created in collaboration with Student Government and open to all.
cards.access_notes: UC Libraries describes the room as open to all; follow library conduct and building-access policies.

cards.title: AACRC Quiet Study
cards.subtitle: African American Cultural & Resource Center
cards.notes: Bring a project group for collaborative work using the flexible tables, projector screen, dry-erase board, or desktop computers; this student space is not reservable.
cards.short_summary: A student-centered collaborative study room with flexible seating and presentation tools.
cards.evidence_claim: The AACRC says its Quiet Study is a dedicated space for students to study and work collaboratively and lists flexible seating, computers, a projector screen, and dry-erase board.
cards.access_notes: UC says the Quiet Study is not reservable; respect the Center’s student-focused use and posted expectations.

cards.title: AACRC Student Lounge
cards.subtitle: African American Cultural & Resource Center
cards.notes: Stop in to decompress or meet peers, using the lounge’s seating and shared amenities while keeping the space available for the community it serves.
cards.short_summary: A student lounge for relaxing, meeting other students, and building community.
cards.evidence_claim: The AACRC states that its Student Lounge is dedicated to students and serves as a place to relax, meet other students, and build community.
cards.access_notes: UC says the Student Lounge is not reservable; follow Center guidance and posted expectations.

cards.title: C.A.T.S. Lounge
cards.subtitle: Seventh floor, Steger Student Life Center
cards.notes: Check the lounge for student-organization meetings, collaborative projects, informal gatherings, or its scheduled programming and activities.
cards.short_summary: A flexible seventh-floor hub for programming, meetings, projects, and informal gatherings.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Student Affairs describes the C.A.T.S. Lounge as a central gathering hub that hosts student-organization meetings, collaborative projects, informal gatherings, and social events.
cards.access_notes: Located on the seventh floor of Steger Student Life Center; programming and room use may vary.

cards.title: Commuter Student Lounge
cards.subtitle: Room 645, sixth floor, Steger Student Life Center
cards.notes: If you commute, use the tables, charging outlets, microwaves, printer, and whiteboard as a between-class base; enter SSLC across from Center Court and go to floor six.
cards.short_summary: A commuter-focused lounge with study, charging, food-storage, and connection resources.
cards.evidence_claim: UC lists seating, tables, charging outlets, games, a whiteboard, sink, microwaves, and printer in the Commuter Student Lounge, and provides directions to Room 645.
cards.access_notes: UC lists current lounge hours as 8 a.m.–6 p.m., Monday–Friday; it is a commuter-student resource.

cards.title: Bearcat’s Den
cards.subtitle: Room 539, Steger Student Life Center near TUC
cards.notes: Drop by for its ongoing activities, small-group workshops, or wellness-and-community programs; enter from MainStreet near TUC and look for Room 539.
cards.short_summary: A Student Affairs space for activities, workshops, and programs centered on wellness and community.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Student Affairs says Bearcat’s Den in Room 539 offers ongoing activities, including small-group workshops and programs that promote wellness and community.
cards.access_notes: UC directs visitors to enter from MainStreet near TUC; activities and programs vary.
